svg.text: Each key is a switch and a diode. Each node Kn has two more diodes (charlie and interrupt) in the diode array.
1. Scan path of one key (from_net = Pa, to_net = Kj)
the switch and key diode to Kj.
3. The charlie diode lets Pj read it.
2. Key at each (drive pin, node) pair: 31 of 42 slots
Rules: each (Pa, Kj) pair is used once, and a ≠ j. A pin cannot read its own node.
A column uses one pin in both halves (P1..P5). Each half uses one node per row.
Left: r1 = K6, r2 = K7, r3 and thumbs = K1. Right: r1 = K2, r2 = K3, r3 and thumbs = K5.
Four keys use K4 because their pin equals the row node. The encoder uses P6 → K7.
Keys per node: K1..K5 have 4 keys each, K6 has 5, K7 has 6 (5 keys + encoder).
ZMK kscan: gpios = P1..P7, interrupt-gpios = INT, RC(row, col) = (from − 1, to − 1).
3. Where the keys sit on the board (color = node, label = pin → node)
Keys are drawn at their real position and angle. ★ = key that uses K4. The diode array and MCU are on the back of the board.
